title: Vincent van Gogh
description: The Dutch master—fame, struggle, and a single sale that echoes through art history.

questions.question: Which Dutch painter created 'The Starry Night' in 1889 while living at an asylum in Saint-Rémy?
questions.explanation: He painted it by day from the view out his barred window, inventing the village below. He later told Émile Bernard it was a failure: "reaching for stars that are too big."

questions.question: Famously, how many paintings is van Gogh said to have sold during his lifetime?
questions.explanation: That's the legend, and only one sale is documented beyond doubt. Letters hint at a few more, but nearly all of his roughly 860 oil paintings went unsold while he lived.

questions.question: What is the title of that one documented painting van Gogh sold while alive?
questions.explanation: He painted it from memory in November 1888, after a Sunday walk with Gauguin. He told Theo they'd seen "a red vineyard, all red like red wine."

questions.question: Who bought 'The Red Vineyard' at an 1890 Brussels show—a fellow painter whose brother Van Gogh had once painted?
questions.explanation: The only woman in Belgium's avant-garde group Les XX, she was refreshingly unsentimental, writing to her brother: "It will look good in a corner of the living room."

questions.question: How much did Anna Boch pay for 'The Red Vineyard' in 1890?
questions.explanation: About 400 francs (some accounts say 350). Five months later Vincent was dead. Boch later sold it for many times that, and it now hangs in Moscow's Pushkin Museum.
